newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed higher on Friday, dragged out of a day-long depression caused by a Heineken profit warning after unexpectedly encouraging U.S. economic data boosted Wall Street to a new trading high.
"The economic figures which came out of the U.S. this afternoon were extremely positive for inflation that's why the market went up by the close," one dealer said.

The AEX index closed 1.15 points up at 566.05, clawing its way back from a session low of 558.25 reached as Heineken fell more than 50 guilders to 312.00. By the close short covering saw Heineken rally to 322.50, down 40.20 guilders on the day.
Heineken sent the market reeling with its pre-opening announcement of lower than expected first half net profit and forecast of 1996 net below 1995's 664 million guilders.

The company said poor spring weather in Europe had held back beer sales in the region, hampering profits in the first half which rose six percent to 297 million guilders, below analysts' forecasts of 308 to 322 million guilders.

Analysts cut their forecasts for the full year and some said they expected Heineken shares to fall further on Monday. "It's possible if there are a lot of news items tomorrow that there will be some more selling pressure next week," said a trader.

"We think another 20 guilder fall (in Heineken shares) on Monday is possible, unfortunately," the trader said. The results and profit warning triggered a wave of activity with over 3.7 million shares changing hands compared to a more usual daily turnover of between 200,000 and 400,000 shares.
Dealers said news the August U.S. consumer price index showed a rise of 0.1 percent against expectations of a 0.2 percent rise saved the AEX from closing sharply down.
"You could have expected the market to be up three or four points on the Wall Street rise so you can see the impact of Heineken," one trader said.
Dealers said Wall Street surged because the data pointed to weak inflation, convincing some investors there would be no hike in interest rates at the Fed's September 24 policy meeting.

The Wall Street rally clipped back an early 3.50 guilder loss in Unilever to 60 cents at 264.00 by the close. The early fall had eroded some of the week's 16 guilder gain after last week's restructuring remarks from its new UK chairman.

Dealers said some of the shine came off the stock after reports Unilever "clarified" media comments about growth, saying Niall FitzGerald did not say a reported profit growth target of 10 percent would take place this year and next.
Brewer Grolsch was hurt by the tide of Heineken selling, slipping 2.10 guilders to 67.00 in sympathy.
Financials were boosted by the gain in bond prices following the U.S. data with ABN AMRO up 1.40 guilders to 93.40 and ING 1.60 guilders stronger at 52.90.
Cyclicals were again in favour with DSM 4.50 guilders higher at 167.00 and Akzo 1.30 up at 194.00 guilders. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
